_question: Oksijenin yukseltgen mi verici mi oldugu FILOGENIDEN ya da yapi tahmininden cikarilabilir mi?
_answer: NO. The signal measured here is real and entirely trivial.

where_the_cross_type_signal_comes_from.note: Every cross-type neighbouring of identically labelled enzymes comes from a single orthologue pair: Nvd and DAF36, both cholesterol 7-desaturases. RedG -- the only independent oxidant_only type -- sits nowhere near them.

why_it_cannot_predict: The signal says no more than 'orthologues of the same enzyme sit together on a tree', which is the ordinary behaviour of sequence similarity rather than information about the label.
The positive class is n=3 and two of the three are orthologues, so the number of independent observations is 2. No rule built on that many positives is falsifiable.

Where the oxygen goes depends on the substrate and the chemistry, not on the fold: all 76 types carry the same fold and the same cofactor pair (they pass the motif gate) and yet they spread across four different oxygen fates. A structure prediction can say that the cofactor centre is intact -- which is what we already use it for -- but it cannot say what the substrate is, and without the substrate the fate of the oxygen cannot be known.
